scope: backend/src/swarm/judge-session.ts (judgeSession() guard block: active-status, role, take-conflict, third_party_enabled gate, #918 operator exemption)
backend/src/api/routes/swarm-admin.ts (admin authorization gate for role-grant and member-update routes)
#922 diff: judgedBy/judgedByMemberId exposure through the admin API/panel
verdict: One medium-severity finding confirms and sharpens already-filed issue #925: the self-service 'operator' field forges the trust signal judge-session.ts uses to exempt in-house judges from the #796 third-party gate, requiring only a routine (not unusual) admin role grant to become live. Two low/info secondary findings (untested take-conflict guard, thin self-service audit trail). All other examined authorization, race, and lifecycle boundaries held up under adversarial testing.

findings.requirement: docs/decisions.md:3301-3341 (#796 amendment: third-party judging gated behind an admin-flippable, off-by-default flag, independent of role grant)
findings.impact: Any active member can self-declare operator='robotmoney' via the unrestricted self-service profile route, with no role or admin check. judge-session.ts's #918 exemption reads this field fresh on every judging attempt and grants the in-house exemption to any row carrying that value, regardless of who set it. Combined with a routine (not unusual) admin grant of role:'judge' -- the same action #796/#812 document as the normal path for a legitimate external judge -- an unvetted, self-registered member's model-authored opinion can bypass the third_party_enabled gate entirely, landing in swarm_recommendation in enforce mode or accumulating trusted-looking history in shadow mode, without the admin's separate documented decision to permit third-party judging ever being made. The self-service audit row records no field values (finding 003), so the forgery is stealthy by default.
findings.recommendation: Remove operator from self-service PROFILE_KEYS (admin-only, like handle) or refuse reserved values (at minimum 'robotmoney') in validateMemberProfile(); and/or re-key judge-session.ts's exemption off LIVE_ROSTER_HANDLES membership rather than the free-text operator column. Add the regression test named in this finding's evidence trail (a judge-role member self-declaring operator via updateMemberProfile must still be refused third_party_judging_disabled while the flag is off).

findings.requirement: docs/decisions.md:3283-3291 (#812: a judge with a take in the session it judges must be refused, to keep the judge free of a market view)
findings.impact: The judge_member_has_take_in_session refusal has no test anywhere in backend/tests/ (confirmed by repository-wide grep for its exact error string, which matches only the definition site). The guard's logic is correct on direct inspection, but a future edit could silently weaken, invert, or misscope this one-line check with no red test to catch the regression.
findings.recommendation: Add a test: promote a member with an existing take in session S from role='member' to role='judge', then call judgeSession(S, { judgeMemberId }) and assert a 409 judge_member_has_take_in_session with no judgement row written.

findings.impact: updateMemberProfile()'s audit row logs only {memberId}, unlike updateMemberAdminTx's audit row which logs the changed field names (and old/new value for a handle change). Now that operator carries authorization significance (finding 001), an admin cannot reconstruct from the audit log alone whether or when a member's operator value was ever forged, compounding finding 001's stealthiness. No capability is granted by this gap on its own.
findings.recommendation: Log fields: Object.keys(patch) on the self-service update_profile audit row, mirroring the admin path.

clean_areas: Admin route authorization (X-Admin-Token / isPrivileged()) is fail-closed and checked before any request body is parsed or database touched, across all /api/swarm/admin/* routes (backend/src/api/routes/swarm-admin.ts:1-7).

The 60-second model-call race window for judge status/role/third_party_enabled is correctly closed: all three checks run inside judgeSession()'s write transaction, after the model call returns, under a per-session pg_advisory_xact_lock (backend/src/swarm/judge-session.ts:219-278), directly exercised by backend/tests/swarm-judge-third-party-flag.test.ts's fresh-read test.

judgeSessionAdmin's out-of-transaction resolution of Themis's id by handle (admin.ts:1214-1227) is safe: the transaction's own SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on that exact id re-verifies status/role/operator fresh, so a concurrent revocation between the two reads is caught with a correctly-attributed refusal, never a misleading generic error.
The take-conflict guard's transaction ordering (model call outside the transaction, conflict check inside it after the advisory lock) is structurally correct, though untested (finding 002).

Member handle/id namespace collision is enforced at the database level by an ENABLE ALWAYS trigger (migration 0031) surviving pg_restore --disable-triggers and logical replication; self-service cannot set handle at all, so a member cannot rename itself to 'themis' to hijack judgeSessionAdmin's handle-based resolution.
applyOpinion() never writes weights/quorum/stances -- confirmed by direct reading of its merge object literal (judge-session.ts:368-431), matching the module's documented invariant.
swarm_session_judgements and swarm_members are both covered by the append-only guard (backend/src/db/append-only-guard.ts:212,221).

memberIdForToken() correctly joins on status='active' (issue #799 fix), and submitRecommendation() independently refuses any role='judge' member from submitting a take at all, which is the primary defense the take-conflict guard backs up for the narrower promoted-after-submission case.

seedLiveRoster()'s idempotent upsert correctly preserves an admin's later role grant/revocation across re-seeds (commit 4c57cef3) while still refreshing operator from the manifest for the three named seats.
unresolved_decisions: Which of issue #925's two proposed fixes (remove operator from self-service entirely, vs. reserve specific values) is the intended remediation direction.

Whether the public roster route's verbatim rendering of a self-declared operator (a display-only reputational-forgery surface noted in issue #925's own text) needs independent remediation; no other backend authorization decision was found to read operator besides judge-session.ts.
limitations: judge.ts's prompt construction and the full take/brief-to-model-call content flow were not separately re-audited for prompt-injection beyond confirming the weights-are-never-written invariant by direct inspection.
#922's frontend admin panel changes were reviewed only for new privileged-data exposure (none found), not for XSS/rendering correctness.
CORS/cross-origin implications (D43) were out of scope.
The test suite was not executed; 'no test exists' claims are based on grep-verified absence of relevant assertions/error strings across backend/tests/, not a red run.
worker/handlers/swarm.ts's cron scheduling logic was reviewed only far enough to confirm it calls the same judgeSessionAdmin() entry point audited above.
unreviewed_surfaces: judge.ts's model prompt-injection surface beyond the weights-invariant check.
